name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Skillet
writer_notes: SOURCE YIELD 4, rebuilt to 14 at the mapper's 3.5x scale. Every gram and buy string transcribed from mapped\creamy-tuscan-chicken-skillet.json; no number computed in prose.

MACROS transcribed from the mapper's food-macros-db recompute at 14 servings and re-verified by the writer with the build guard's own formula: 518 cal, 46 g protein, 9 g carbs, 33 g fat per serving (raw 517.8 / 45.9 / 8.8 / 32.9). In band for this run: 518 cal inside [400, 650] with 132 cal of ceiling headroom, and 9 g carbs well under the 35 g gate. The source's own published 485 cal / 42 g protein / 8 g carbs / 32 g fat tracks these within the 15 percent instrument (our chicken books at the house 200 g each-weight versus the source's implied ~173 g/serving).

SUN-DRIED TOMATOES BASIS: the line books to the NEW oil-packed food-macros-db row (Sun-Dried Tomatoes (Oil-Packed), USDA 11955 drained, 213 cal / 23.3 C per 100 g, cup = 110 g), which the mapper added and used for its verified numbers. The DRY row (Sun-Dried Tomatoes, cup = 54 g, ~257 cal / 55.7 C per 100 g) would halve the grams and nearly double the carb density and is REFUTED by the mapper for this carb-gated run. The oil-packed item name has a macro row but NO db\ingredients.json bid row, so the price side is BLOCKED (see run report); the plain-name bid sun-dried-tomatoes is the correct board commodity and must be wired to the oil-packed item name through the match-soundness gate before this recipe can cost and publish.

SPINACH is FRESH per the source and the mapper (macro row 'Spinach' is the fresh USDA row, 23 cal / 100 g). The legacy db\ingredients.json bid for item 'Spinach' still points at frozen-chopped-spinach, a fresh-to-frozen price-class defect the mapper flagged; prose names fresh spinach (the recipe of record) and the bid needs correcting to the live fresh 'spinach' commodity through the gate. Macro side is unaffected (fresh and frozen rows are per-gram identical). RESOLVED 2026-08-16: the bid was corrected. Item Spinach now bids the fresh weekly commodity spinach (priced 7/7 stores, cheapest Walmart $0.20/oz, a 10 oz bag of fresh leaf); the frozen recipes keep the separate Frozen Chopped Spinach row. Cost block re-rendered off the fresh basis.

EVERY BOUGHT INGREDIENT IS USED BY A STEP and no step uses anything unbought: chicken (steps 2,3,6,7), paprika (2), garlic powder (2), salt (2), butter (3), heavy cream (4), sun-dried tomatoes (4), garlic (4), spinach (5). Walked the costed list against the steps both directions.

SHOP_SMART makes NO leftover, per-ounce, or lasts-several-batches claim, so no bullet needs a cost_lines entry to prove it; every statement is grounded in the recipe's own buy amount and package form. Re-walk the bullets against cost_lines once the recipe costs.
GARLIC POWDER grams 10.9 rounds to 11 g at build (int); a fractional gram is not a cook measure and the macro impact is under 1 cal/serving.
intro_html: Tuscan chicken sounds like a restaurant order, but it is really just seared chicken finished in a cream sauce with sun-dried tomatoes and spinach. No long braise, no special cut, no equipment you do not already own. You season the cutlets, brown them in butter, then build the sauce right in the same pan and let the two finish together. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 10 grams of carbs. That is a creamy, rich-tasting dinner that still lands inside a low-carb week.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 14 thin sliced chicken breasts (about 6.2 lb) (2800 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 14 thin sliced chicken breasts (about 6.2 lb): ~$13.77. Buy 7 lbs: $15.61.
Sun-Dried Tomatoes (Oil-Packed), 1 3/4 cups oil-packed, drained: ~$3.59. Buy 1 24oz jar: $12.65.
Pantry seasonings (paprika, garlic powder, salt): ~$0.27. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $23.42 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.67 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $38.77 across 14 servings, roughly $2.77 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $2.78 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $41.55. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for a creamy Tuscan chicken dinner that tastes like it came off a restaurant menu. The chicken and the cream carry it; the sun-dried tomatoes and spinach just make it look and taste expensive.
shop_smart: Fourteen thin chicken cutlets are the backbone. That is one per serving, and it is where most of the money and all of the protein live. Reach for the big family pack of boneless skinless breasts instead of the small trays so you are paying for chicken, not packaging, and slice any thick breasts flat yourself.

Heavy cream is what makes it Tuscan. You need about three and a half cups. Buy the real heavy cream, not half-and-half and not the light stuff, because the fat is what lets the sauce reduce and cling to the chicken instead of breaking.

Oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes carry the flavor. Grab the jar packed in oil rather than the dry bag, and drain the oil off before they go in the pan. About one and three quarter cups drained gives the sauce its deep, sweet-tart backbone.

Fresh spinach wilts in at the very end. You want about three and a half cups chopped. A regular bag or bunch of fresh spinach cooks down fast and folds green through the sauce. This is fresh spinach, not the frozen block.

Butter, garlic, and three pantry spices round it out. A little butter to sear in, a few cloves of garlic, and paprika, garlic powder, and salt for the rub. These are backbone staples you most likely already have, so they barely move the cart.
make_it: Weigh your empty skillet and write the number down. You will use it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight instead of eyeballing every container.
Combine the paprika, garlic powder, and salt in a small bowl, then sprinkle the mix evenly over both sides of the chicken cutlets to coat.

Melt the butter in a large, heavy skillet over medium heat. Working in batches so the pan is not crowded, add the cutlets and cook about 5 minutes a side until browned and cooked through. Move the chicken to a plate and set it aside.
Pour the heavy cream into the same pan and add the drained sun-dried tomatoes and the minced garlic. Stir well and let the sauce cook over low heat about 2 minutes to start thickening.
Add the chopped spinach and stir it in. Keep cooking over low heat until the spinach has wilted and the sauce has thickened, about 3 minutes.
Return the chicken and any collected juices to the pan and turn each piece to coat it in the sauce.

Weigh the full pan and subtract the empty weight from Step 1 to get the cooked total. Divide by 14 and give each container one cutlet and an even share of the creamy tomato and spinach sauce, aiming for that weight.
portion_html: Set the full pan on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the cooked total. Divide that number by 14. Each container gets one chicken cutlet and an even spoonful of the creamy tomato and spinach sauce, landing near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

head.description: Creamy Tuscan chicken for meal prep: seared chicken cutlets finished in a cream sauce with sun-dried tomatoes and spinach, built for 14 servings. About {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, with under 10 grams of carbs.
head.keywords: tuscan chicken, creamy tuscan chicken, low carb meal prep, high protein chicken dinner, sun dried tomato chicken skillet
recipeIngredient: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 14 thin sliced chicken breasts (about 6.2 lb) (2800 g)
Sun-Dried Tomatoes (Oil-Packed), 1 3/4 cups oil-packed, drained (193 g)
steps: Combine the paprika, garlic powder, and salt and season the chicken cutlets on both sides.
Melt the butter in a large skillet and sear the cutlets in batches until browned and cooked through, then set them aside.
Add the heavy cream, drained sun-dried tomatoes, and garlic to the pan and simmer to thicken.
Stir in the chopped spinach and cook until wilted and the sauce has thickened.
Return the chicken to the pan and coat it in the sauce.
Weigh the pan, subtract the empty weight, and divide across 14 containers.
